formulas.name: Central limit theorem statement (as printed)
formulas.expression: Xi IID => SUM(Xi) ~ N(mu,sigma)
formulas.conditions: used to motivate why the normal distribution is prevalent for process outputs

formulas.name: Process capability index Cpk
formulas.expression: C_pk = min( (X_U - mu)/(3*sigma) , (mu - X_L)/(3*sigma) )
formulas.conditions: X ~ N(mu,sigma); slide shows X_U - X_L = 6*sigma giving Cpk=1 (99.73% conform, 0.27% defective) and X_U - X_L = 8*sigma giving Cpk=1.33 (99.9937% conform, 63 ppm defective)

formulas.name: Normal distribution in Excel
formulas.expression: phi(x1) = 1/(sigma*sqrt(2*pi)) * exp(-(x1-mu)^2/(2*sigma^2)) = NORM.DIST(x1,mu,sigma,FALSE); Phi(x2) = INTEGRAL_{-inf}^{x2} phi(x) dx = NORM.DIST(x2,mu,sigma,TRUE); x2 = Phi^-1(p) = X_p = NORM.INV(p,mu,sigma)
formulas.conditions: to generate a pseudo-random normal sample: =NORM.INV(RAND(),MU,SIGMA)

formulas.name: Probability of i non-conformities in a lot (binomial)
formulas.expression: P[i] = C_N^i * pi^i * (1-pi)^(N-i)

symbols.i: number of non-conforming items in the lot
symbols.C_N^i: number of combinations of N items taken i at a time

formulas.conditions: defects occur independently over time (stable process)

formulas.name: SRS sampling distribution of number of defectives (hypergeometric, binomial approximation)
formulas.expression: P[d=i] = (C_D^i * C_(N-D)^(n-i)) / C_N^n  ~=  C_n^i * pi^i * (1-pi)^(n-i)  (binomial)

symbols.d: number of defectives found in the sample
symbols.D: number of defectives in the lot

formulas.conditions: exact distribution is hypergeometric; binomial approximation is used unless the population is small

formulas.name: Sampling variance of P (SRS, binomial)
formulas.expression: sigma^2[P] = pi*(1-pi)/n

formulas.name: Pre-stratified sample: unbiasedness and variance of the combined estimator
formulas.expression: E[P] = E[P_s] = pi;  sigma^2[P_s] = (W_A*sigma_A^2 + W_B*sigma_B^2)/n;  sigma^2[P] = (W_A*sigma_A^2 + W_B*sigma_B^2 + W_A*W_B*(pi_A-pi_B)^2)/n
formulas.conditions: proportional pre-stratification: n_A = W_A*n, n_B = W_B*n

formulas.name: General two-stratum mean/variance decomposition (used to derive the stratification formulas)
formulas.expression: mu = W_A*mu_A + W_B*mu_B;  sigma^2 = W_A*sigma_A^2 + W_B*sigma_B^2 + W_A*(mu_A-mu)^2 + W_B*(mu_B-mu)^2
formulas.conditions: given in the notes as the general identity behind the page-17 formulas

formulas.name: Optimal vs proportional pre-stratification sample allocation
formulas.expression: n_A = (W_A*sigma_A)/(W_A*sigma_A + W_B*sigma_B) * n  (idem for n_B), with sigma_A = sqrt(pi_A*(1-pi_A)) (idem sigma_B). Proportional stratification: n_A/n_B = W_A/W_B. Optimal stratification: n_A/n_B = (W_A*sigma_A)/(W_B*sigma_B)

symbols.n_A: sample size drawn from stratum A
symbols.n_B: sample size drawn from stratum B

formulas.conditions: optimal stratification requires prior knowledge of pi_A, pi_B (e.g. via a prior sample from each stratum)

formulas.name: Distribution of the number of defectives in a (pre-)stratified sample
formulas.expression: P[d_s=i] = SUM_{k=0}^{i} [ C_nA^k * piA^k * (1-piA)^(nA-k) * C_nB^(i-k) * piB^(i-k) * (1-piB)^(nB-i+k) ]

symbols.d_s: number of defectives in the stratified sample

formulas.conditions: based on binomial probabilities within each stratum; hypergeometric to be exact

formulas.name: Two equally-sized normally distributed strata: variance of the population and of the sample mean
formulas.expression: sigma^2 = sigma_S^2 + (mu_A-mu_B)^2/4;  E[Xbar] = E[Xbar_S] = mu;  sigma^2[Xbar_S] = sigma_S^2/n;  sigma^2[Xbar] = sigma^2[Xbar_S] + (mu_A-mu_B)^2/(4n)

symbols.Xbar: SRS sample mean (printed as X with an overline)

formulas.conditions: two equally sized strata (W_A=W_B=1/2), each normally distributed, same variance sigma_S^2, different means

formulas.name: Cluster-sampling probability of zero defectives (worked extreme-concentration case)

symbols.d_C: number of defectives found in the cluster sample
symbols.C_9^2: ways to pick 2 of the 9 defect-free palettes
symbols.C_10^2: ways to pick 2 of the 10 palettes
symbols.C_100^5: ways to pick 5 of the 100 boxes on a palette
symbols.C_80^5: ways to pick 5 defect-free boxes out of the 80 defect-free boxes on the one palette that holds all 20 defective boxes

formulas.conditions: extreme case: all 200 defectives in the lot are concentrated in 20 boxes of a single palette (out of 10 palettes of 100 boxes); cluster plan = 2 palettes drawn at random, 5 boxes drawn at random from each

formulas.name: Long-run equivalence of SRS and cluster-sample binomial probabilities (3-defectives example)
formulas.conditions: shown to illustrate that, when the lots come from a stable process with a given pi, cluster sampling and SRS give the same (binomial) sampling distribution in the long run

formulas.name: Non-response bias / variance of the sample mean
formulas.expression: sigma^2[Xbar] = sigma^2/n
formulas.conditions: used to explain that sampling error (random) and bias (systematic, from an unrepresentative frame) both contribute to total error; a small SRS from the full population can beat a large SRS from a biased frame

formulas.name: Single-stage sampling plan for attributes - OC curve
formulas.expression: OC(p) = P(X<=c | p) = H(c;N,M_p,n) with M_p = [N*p]

symbols.M_p: number of defectives in the lot = [N*p] (nearest integer)

formulas.conditions: AQL = p such that OC(p) = 1-alpha (=95% stated as the default); LQL = p such that OC(p) = beta (=10% stated as the default). Specifying both AQL and LQL uniquely characterizes the (n,c) plan.

formulas.name: Double sampling plan for attributes - OC, Pi(p), ASN(p)

symbols.Pi(p): probability of reaching a decision after the first sample

formulas.conditions: as printed; the first OC(p) term uses 'H' as the population-size argument of H(.), which is inconsistent with the N used in the Pi(p) formula directly below (see ambiguities)

formulas.name: SPRT likelihood ratio and log-likelihood (Wald sequential probability ratio test)
formulas.expression: Lambda(X_n,n;p0,pt) = (pt/p0)^X_n * ((1-pt)/(1-p0))^(n-X_n);  log(Lambda) = X_n*( log(pt/p0) - log((1-pt)/(1-p0)) ) + n*log((1-p0)/(1-pt))

symbols.X_n: number of defectives found after n inspections
symbols.pt: LQL fraction defective (course also writes p1/pt)

formulas.conditions: stop and accept if log(Lambda) < log(A) (A = beta/(1-alpha) < 1); stop and reject if log(Lambda) > log(B) (B = (1-beta)/alpha > 1); PR = 1-OC(p0) = alpha (producer's risk), CR = OC(pt) = beta (consumer's risk). For binomial instead of hypergeometric, OK if lot size is large compared to sample size.

formulas.name: SPRT reject/accept boundaries (graphical form Xn vs n)
formulas.expression: Reject: X_n >= h2 + s*n, with h2 = log((1-beta)/alpha) / log( pt*(1-p0) / (p0*(1-pt)) )  and  s = log((1-p0)/(1-pt)) / log( pt*(1-p0) / (p0*(1-pt)) ), both > 0.  Accept: X_n <= -h1 + s*n, with h1 = log((1-alpha)/beta) / log( pt*(1-p0) / (p0*(1-pt)) ) > 0

symbols.s: common slope of the accept/reject lines

formulas.conditions: example given: p0=0.01, pt=0.05, alpha=beta=0.05 => h1=h2=1.78 and s=0.025

formulas.name: SPRT OC and ASN functions
formulas.expression: p(tau) = [1 - ((1-pt)/(1-p0))^tau] / [ (pt/p0)^tau - ((1-pt)/(1-p0))^tau ];  ASN(p) = { [OC(p)*log(beta/(1-alpha)) + (1-OC(p))*log((1-beta)/alpha)] / [p*log(pt/p0) + (1-p)*log((1-pt)/(1-p0))]  if p != s ;  h1*h2/(s*(1-s))  if p = s };  OC(p(tau)) = [ ((1-beta)/alpha)^tau - 1 ] / [ ((1-beta)/alpha)^tau - (beta/(1-alpha))^tau ]

symbols.tau: parameter indexing points on the OC curve (tau=-infinity: p(tau)=1; tau=-1: p(tau)=pt; tau=0: p(tau)=s in [p0,pt]; tau=1: p(tau)=p0; tau=+infinity: p(tau)=0)

formulas.conditions: given without proof; verifiable by simulation with the course's R-function OC_SPRT.TXT

formulas.name: Single sampling plan for variables - inspection statistic and OC curve
formulas.expression: Q = (Xbar - xi)/s;  accept the lot if Q >= k  <=>  Xbar - k*s >= xi;  OC(p) ~= 1 - Phi( (z_p+k)*sqrt(n) / (1+k^2/2)^(1/2) )

symbols.k: acceptance constant (counterpart of c for attribute plans)
symbols.z_p: standard-normal quantile for fraction defective p

formulas.conditions: lot acceptable if p <= AQL = p0 <=> xi <= X_p0; given n, k can be found so that OC(AQL=p0) = 1-alpha: k ~= t(1-alpha,p0,n)

formulas.name: Variable sampling plan: k and n from AQL and LQL
formulas.expression: k = (z_pt*z_alpha + z_p0*z_beta) / (z_(1-alpha) + z_(1-beta));  n = (z_(1-alpha)+z_(1-beta))^2 * (1+k^2/2) / (z_pt - z_p0)^2
formulas.conditions: derivation left as an exercise; worked example: (p0=0.5%, 1-alpha=95%) and (pt=3.5%, beta=5%) => k=2.1939, n=64

formulas.name: Variable-sampling k-factor t(alpha,beta,n) (main-deck derivation)
formulas.expression: t(alpha,beta,n) = [ Z_(1-beta) + Z_(1-alpha)*sqrt( 1/n + Z^2_(1-beta)/(2n) - Z^2_(1-alpha)/(2n^2) ) ] / [ 1 - Z^2_(1-alpha)/(2n) ];  hence t(1-alpha,p0,n) = [ Z_(1-p0) + Z_alpha*sqrt( 1/n + Z^2_(1-p0)/(2n) - Z^2_alpha/(2n^2) ) ] / [ 1 - Z^2_alpha/(2n) ]
formulas.conditions: valid for sufficiently large n; used so that with probability 1-alpha at least a fraction 1-beta of the population is >= Xbar - k*s

formulas.name: Rectifying inspection: AOQ, AOQL, ATI
formulas.expression: AOQ(p) = p*OC(p)*(1 - (n/N)*R_s*) ~= p*OC(p)  [for n<<N], with R_s* = H(c-1;N-1,[Np]-1,n-1) / H(c;N,[Np],n);  AOQL(p) = max_p AOQ(p);  ATI(p) = n*OC(p) + N*(1-OC(p))
formulas.conditions: assumes non-destructive tests, defectives found are replaced by good ones, and rejected lots undergo full rectification (100% inspection with replacement); formula for R_s* assumes single-stage sampling

formulas.name: Skip-lot qualification probability (worked example)
formulas.expression: P_q = B(3;640,p) * B^2(0;80,p)   (B = binomial c.d.f.)

symbols.P_q: probability of qualifying for the skip-lot state
symbols.p: overall probability of producing a defective item

formulas.conditions: worked example: plan (80,2) on lots of size 1000, AQL=1%, assuming the last 10 lots were accepted; condition = first 8 samples have <=3 defectives total AND last two samples are defect-free

formulas.name: Deming's inspection criterion - total quality cost

symbols.k2: unit cost of an assembly failure (dismantle/repair/reassemble)
symbols.Q: probability of accepting a lot on average (= OC(p))
symbols.p'': average fraction defectives in lots passing inspection

formulas.conditions: parts delivered in lots of size N, single-stage attribute plan (n,Ac); rejected lots are screened and fully rectified; assumes k1 << k2

formulas.name: Deming's break-even rule
formulas.expression: if p < k1/k2 then TC is minimal for n=0 (no inspection); if p > k1/k2 then TC is minimal for n=N (screening); k1/k2 is called the break-even quality
formulas.conditions: proved via an R-function referenced as DEMING.TXT in the course; assumes the process is stable at percentage defectives p

formulas.name: Deming's model - Q and p'' as sums over the lot's defect count D
formulas.expression: Q = OC(p) = SUM_{D=0}^{N} pi_D * beta_D ;  p'' = SUM_{D=0}^{N} (pi_D/beta_D) * SUM_{j=0}^{Ac} beta_j*(D-j)/(N-n)  >  SUM_{D=0}^{N} (pi_D/beta_D) * SUM_{j=0}^{Ac} beta_j*D/N = SUM_{D=0}^{N} pi_D*D/N = p

symbols.pi_D: probability of exactly D defectives in the lot = binomial = b(D;N,p)
symbols.beta_D: probability of accepting a lot with D defectives = hypergeometric = H(Ac;N,D,n)

formulas.conditions: shown to demonstrate p'' > p, i.e. lots that pass inspection are on average worse than the incoming lot quality p; see course R-functions OC_SAI.TXT and OQ_SAI.TXT

stated_answers.note: at Cpk=1.33 there will in practice never be more than 3 non-conform items in lots of size 10000

conventions.as_stated: AQL : acceptable quality level - should normally pass the inspection. LQL : limiting quality level (LTPD : lot tolerance percent defectives) - should normally be rejected. (Further Reading, p.2: 'Acceptable quality is described by the number AQL (acceptable quality level), while unacceptable quality is described by the number LQL (limiting quality level, synonym : LTPD = lot tolerance percent defectives). AQL and LQL should be agreed upon by both the parties involved.')

conventions.topic: Producer's risk and consumer's risk definitions
conventions.as_stated: Main deck diagram (p.23): 'Producer's risk : risk of rejecting a good lot. Consumer's risk : risk of accepting a good lot.' Further Reading (p.2) states it more precisely: 'producer's risk (risk of rejecting a lot of good quality = type-I error) and consumer's risk (risk of accepting a lot of bad quality = type-II error).'

conventions.topic: Default alpha/beta for constructing an (n,c) plan from AQL and LQL (Peach method)
conventions.as_stated: AQL = p such that OC(p) = 1 - alpha (= 95 %). LQL = p such that OC(p) = beta (= 10 %). 'normally alpha = 5%... In the same way for the LQL (LTPD), normally taken beta = 10%.'

conventions.topic: Distribution used for the OC-curve of attribute sampling plans
conventions.as_stated: OC(p) = P(X<=c|p) = H(c;N,Mp,n) with Mp=[Np]; 'H = the hypergeometric c.d.f.' For SPRT: '(For binomial distribution instead of hypergeometric, OK if lot size is large compared to sample size.)'

AOQ(p) = pOC(p)(1-(n/N)Rs*) ~= pOC(p) for n<<N; 'AOQ = Average Outgoing Quality... The maximum value of the AOQ-curve is called the Average Outgoing Quality Limit (AOQL).' 'ATI stands for the Average Total Inspection effort to be made.'

conventions.topic: Excel functions used in the acceptance-sampling workbook
conventions.as_stated: Cells use (with the openpyxl-visible _xlfn. prefix for post-2007 functions): _xlfn.NORM.DIST, _xlfn.NORM.INV, _xlfn.EXPON.DIST, _xlfn.HYPGEOM.DIST, _xlfn.RANK.EQ, _xlfn.STDEV.S, _xlfn.VAR.P, plus legacy COMBIN, RAND, SUMIF, SUMPRODUCT, VLOOKUP/HLOOKUP.

conventions.topic: Variable sampling plan: k factor and sigma known/unknown
conventions.as_stated: 'k is the counterpart of c for a single attributive plan'; the workbook and slides compute s as the sample standard deviation (sigma unknown, estimated from the sample: s = sqrt( 1/(n-1) * SUM(Xi-Xbar)^2 )), and set k ~= t(1-alpha,p0,n).

conventions.topic: sigma estimate used for process capability (Cpk)
conventions.as_stated: 'the actual measurements are taken from a limited process time intervals, i.e., mu and sigma are based on so-called within subgroup calculations. This will be further explained in the section on SPC.'

'Acceptance sampling plans can be found in the ISO-standards 2859 (attributes) and 3951 (variables). These standards have evolved out of the MIL-STD-105 which in turn resulted out of the pioneering work by Harold Dodge and Harry Romig at Bell Labs in the 1920's.' Further Reading p.12 adds: ISO2859 indexes plans by lot size, inspection level (I/II/III), AQL -> Sample Size Code Letter (SSCL) -> sampling plan; severity states normal/tightened/reduced with formal transition rules; sampling procedure can be single/double/multiple/sequential.

Qualification: supplier has a stable manufacturing organisation, continuous production and a certified quality management system, AND 10 consecutive lots are accepted, AND the total number of defective items from the 10 samples is smaller than a given critical level (K&Z table 9.16 p.315), AND the number of defectives in each of the last two lots is smaller than a given critical level (K&Z table 9.17 p.316). Interruption: the number of defectives in a sample is equal to or larger than a given critical level (table 9.17 p.316). Resumption: 4 consecutive lots are accepted AND the number of defectives in each of the last two lots is strictly smaller than a given critical level. Disqualification: the supplier violates the qualification criteria OR within 10 consecutive lots, 2 lots are rejected. Skip-lot inspection probability starts at 0.5, then increases to 0.66(=2/3) and eventually 0.8(=4/5) as quality remains good (diagram shows the complementary inspection probabilities 0.5 -> 0.33 -> 0.2).

'If the process is stable at a given percentage of defectives, then either no inspection or 100% inspection is cost optimal. Deming's assumption is that the production process is stable. Sampling plans do not make this assumption and are designed for catching shifts in process levels.'

conventions.topic: Rounding of n and c (Peach method table lookup)
conventions.as_stated: 'Form R0 = p2/p1 and look for R0 in the table. When the value cannot be found, look for the next larger tabled value.' Example: R0=7 -> tabled value 7.7 used -> c=2, n=164 (approximately confirmed against a chart plan of (160,2)).

ambiguities.issue: Further Reading p.4 states the default convention for constructing a plan from AQL/LQL as OC(p)=beta with beta='10%' by default, but every worked numeric example that uses this method in the same document (pages 4, 5, 7, 8, 9) and the exercise on page 17 actually uses beta=5% (e.g. target points '(0.5%,95%)' and '(3.5%,5%)'). The course does not reconcile the stated default (10%) with the beta=5% used throughout its own examples.

Main-deck diagram on p.23 states 'Consumer's risk : risk of accepting a good lot', which appears to be a typo for 'a bad lot' (it should be the mirror image of producer's risk). The Further Reading document (p.2) gives the standard, non-contradictory definition: 'consumer's risk (risk of accepting a lot of bad quality = type-II error)'. Transcribed exactly as printed in both places.

The double-sampling OC(p) formula on Further Reading p.5 reads 'OC(p) = H(c1;H,Mp,n1) + ...', i.e. the first argument list of H(.) uses the letter 'H' as the population-size argument, instead of 'N' as used consistently everywhere else on the same page (e.g. the Pi(p) formula immediately below: H(c1;N,Mp,n1)). This looks like a printing/typesetting error; transcribed exactly as printed.

Main-deck p.16 body text mixes decimal separators within the same paragraph: 'roughly 1.8x10^241' and '4.3x10^17' are printed with a period as decimal separator, while 'about 9,05x10^58' and 'around 1,4x10^-183' are printed with a comma as decimal separator. Transcribed exactly as printed; readers should not interpret the comma as a thousands separator.
Further Reading p.11 prints 'ALQ = 1 %' where the surrounding text and the rest of the document consistently use 'AQL'. Transcribed exactly as printed (likely a typo for AQL).

Further Reading p.8: the ASN(p) chart for the SPRT worked example (p0=0.005, pt=3.5%, alpha=beta=5%) shows a curve peaking at roughly 150 near p in the 0.01-0.02 range; these values were read off a printed chart (no axis gridline lines up exactly with the peak) rather than given as exact printed numbers, so the precision of 'peak ~150 near p~0.01-0.02' is uncertain.

xlsm sheet 'variable sampling plan': the sample data (F8:F17), the resulting Xbar/s/Q (F4:F6) and the accept/reject decision (I9) are driven by =NORM.INV(RAND(),mu,sigma) and recompute on every recalculation (F9) or file open. The values captured in worked example S04-WE17 (e.g. Xbar=10.372944440560392) are therefore a single non-reproducible snapshot of the live tool, not a fixed course-stated worked example; only C17=0.61 (labeled 'Based on 100 runs') is a stored (non-live) result.

xlsm sheets 'lot fraction defectives' and 'sampling distribution' contain large blocks of live =RAND()-driven formulas (the SRS/pre-stratified/cluster sample columns, and the 10000-row Monte Carlo simulation) that recompute on every recalculation.
